channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Governador do Piauí defende reapresentação de Messias ao Senado
item.description: The Governor of Piauí, Rafael Fonteles (PT), advocated for the re-submission of Union Attorney General Jorge Messias to the Senate for a potential nomination to the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The statement was made in a post on X on Saturday (Feb 2).

item.title: As apostas da família de Carla Zambelli nas eleições de outubro
item.description: The mother of Carla Zambelli, Rita Zambelli, is acting as her political spokesperson while Carla is detained in Italy awaiting extradition. In an Instagram post, Rita endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro as a 'future president' and promoted the pre-candidacy of her other son, Bruno Zambelli, a São Paulo state deputy, for re-election, linking Brazil's hope for freedom to Carla's release, who was convicted for invading the CNJ system. The post also urged followers to join the PL and received over 2,000 likes.

item.title: STF não tem clima para barrar dosimetria no curto prazo
item.description: The PT plans to appeal to the STF to overturn the congressional override of the presidential veto on the Dosimetry Bill (PL 2162/2023), but the Supreme Court currently lacks the appetite for a confrontation with Congress. Ministers prefer to wait for political tensions to subside, particularly after the fallout from the Master case and the recent ruling on the INSS CPI postponement, which signaled the Court’s reluctance to review legislative leadership acts. The outcome will hinge on the randomly assigned rapporteur, as there is no pre-assigned judge, and most ministers avoid escalating inter-branch tensions at this time.

item.title: "Sob controle": Michelle atualiza estado de saúde de Bolsonaro
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro stated that ex-president Jair Bolsonaro had a good night after shoulder surgery and that "everything is under control," per her Instagram post. The rotator cuff repair procedure was performed at DF Star Hospital in Brasília without complications, following authorization from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, supported by the PGR. Bolsonaro, under house arrest, is expected to remain hospitalized for several days for recovery.

item.title: Alcolumbre avisou a Lula em três momentos que Messias seria derrotado no Senado
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre warned President Lula three times in private meetings that Jorge Messias lacked the votes to be confirmed as a Supreme Court justice, but Lula dismissed the warnings, relying on political pressure instead. The choice of Messias strained relations with Alcolumbre, who later worked to secure his defeat after Lula leaked a private conversation between them. The episode exposed poor government coordination and Lula’s unwillingness to pay the political price — such as offering key state-owned company posts — to guarantee Messias’ approval.

item.title: Lula se reuniu zero vezes com líderes do Congresso em 2026
item.description: In 2026, President Lula zeroed formal meetings with Congressional leaders, reflecting a distancing in relations with the Legislature amid political articulation difficulties, highlighted by the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF. The government has prioritized informal encounters, such as Alvorada dinners and campaign team meetings, while the Institutional Relations Secretariat maintains some contact with parliamentarians. The appointment of José Guimarães as minister signals an effort to reorganize Congressional relations, though official meetings with Chamber and Senate presidents remain absent.

item.title: Pré-candidato, Zema defende mudar lei para permitir trabalho infantil no Brasil
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) advocated for changing Brazil's law that prohibits child labor, arguing the ban is a left-wing creation that limits youth opportunities. He cited the U.S., where children can deliver newspapers, and said he would amend current legislation if elected, which today prohibits work for those under 16, allowing only apprenticeship from age 14 under specific rules.

item.title: Roberto Reis na Crusoé: O partido que parou no tempo
item.description: In late March 2026, Lula attempted to explain economic pressures on Brazilian families by citing pet spending and smartphone-driven consumption, but his remarks were seen as out of touch and more like a grandfather’s complaint than economic analysis. The article argues the PT is speaking to a Brazil that no longer exists, accusing the party of being stuck in the past. His comments sparked backlash for sounding elitist and disconnected from citizens’ real struggles.

item.title: Athletico x Grêmio: quais jogadores têm mais chance de fazer gol no confronto do Brasileirão?
item.description: The matchup between Athletico and Grêmio features two in-form strikers: Kevin Viveros of Athletico, with eight goals and leading the Brasileirão scoring chart, and Carlos Vinícius of Grêmio, with seven goals and the Gaúcho team's top scorer this season. Viveros aims to maintain his hot streak to help Athletico push for a G4 spot, while Vinícius seeks redemption after missing three penalties in the Sudamericana. Grêmio holds a slight edge in recent head-to-heads, having won the last two encounters.

item.title: O novo mundo novo (por André Gustavo Stumpf)
item.description: The article criticizes the Workers' Party (PT) for failing to understand Lula's declining popularity, attributing it to the natural wear of a radical populist discourse that hasn't adapted to the digital world. It highlights Brazil's strategic mistake in aligning with Russia in the Ukraine war, risking being on the wrong side of history, and notes Trump's error in underestimating Iran, which led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and a spike in oil prices.

item.title: Michelle atualiza estado de saúde de Bolsonaro após cirurgia: 'Conseguiu tomar sopa'
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro reported that ex-president Jair Bolsonaro is doing well after right shoulder surgery at DF Star Hospital in Brasília. He managed to have soup and regain finger movement, with no complications during the rotator cuff repair procedure. Bolsonaro remains under house arrest, with the surgery approved by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: A primeira viagem de Lula à região Norte em 2026
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is set to travel to the Amazonas in the coming days, marking his first visit to the North region in 2026. The trip comes after he has already visited 23 municipalities across ten states in the country’s other four regions during this election year. The article, available only to subscribers, details the itinerary as part of his campaign agenda.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro nega acordo com Alcolumbre para barrar CPI do Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro denied having made any agreement with Congress President Davi Alcolumbre to block the installation of the CPMI investigating the Banco Master case. In an official statement, he rejected accusations of attempting to obstruct the parliamentary inquiry commission, stating he repudiates any association of his name with such arrangements. The denial comes amid growing political pressure surrounding the investigation into alleged money laundering schemes linked to former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: 'Só lavagem cerebral coletiva explica', diz Haddad sobre empate entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Former minister Fernando Haddad attributed the technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in election polls to a 'collective brainwashing', stating the contrast between the two is so great that only this explanation makes the scenario 'inadmissible'. He made these remarks at a Workers' Day event at Força Sindical in São Paulo, linking the poll results to recent congressional defeats of the Lula government, which he labeled as 'defeats in the fight against corruption', referencing the rejection of Jorge Messias' STF nomination and the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetria bill.

item.title: Juiz nega pedido para remover post de Nikolas sobre Janja
item.description: Judge Júlio César Lérias Ribeiro of the 6th Special Civil Court of Brasília denied a request to remove a social media post by federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira involving First Lady Janja and President Lula. The lawsuit was filed by Manuella Tyler Medrado, first alternate councilwoman of PSOL in Juazeiro (BA). The post originated from content deemed offensive by the plaintiff.

item.title: O risco do "tudo ou nada" de Alcolumbre
item.description: Davi Alcolumbre is taking a high-risk approach by seeking to delay Lula's Supreme Court nomination until after the 2026 elections, banking on a right-wing victory to secure bolsonarist support and his own Senate re-election in 2027. The Planalto is pushing for an immediate appointment, with growing momentum to nominate a woman — which would be historic and a powerful electoral asset for Lula among his female base. Alcolumbre’s gamble could backfire if the Senate is compelled to act, revealing his strategy as politically dangerous and potentially self-defeating.

item.title: ‘Caldeirão com Mion’ define parcerias vocais em nova fase do reality sertanejo
item.description: The show 'Caldeirão com Mion' aired the second episode of the 'Dupla do Brasil' segment, where the six first-voice candidates — Rony, Priscila, Jessyca Paixão, Jessika Dionizio, Luciano Silva, and Bruno Souza — selected their second-voice partners through a harmonization challenge without prior information. With Guilherme & Benuto serving as vocal consultants and Eduardo Pepato as a fixed judge, the six sertanejo duos advancing in the competition were finalized. Benuto emphasized that choosing the second voice is crucial for vocal balance and duo identity, ensuring harmony without direct competition.

item.title: Associação de familiares calcula impacto de lei da dosimetria
item.description: The Association of Relatives and Victims of January 8 (Asfav) estimates that around 600 people could benefit from the dosimetry law, after Congress overturned President Lula's veto. Due to the secrecy of many proceedings at the STF, the figures are only preliminary estimates.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Former Finance Minister and São Paulo gubernatorial pre-candidate Fernando Haddad (PT) emphasized the importance of rest and family time for workers, asserting that Brazil will not collapse under improved labor conditions — just as it did not collapse when vacation time increased from 15 to 30 days or when the 13th salary was introduced. He argued that workers need time to sleep, rest, be with their children, and attend church, countering claims that such demands are unrealistic.

item.title: América se articula para tirar Romário e lançar irmão de Zico à presidência
item.description: Internal discussions at América are underway to replace current president Romário with Edu Coimbra, Zico's older brother and the club's all-time leading scorer with 211 goals, at age 79. The move aims to strengthen leadership with a historically significant and respected figure in Brazilian football, despite the election being scheduled for November. Full access to the article requires a subscription.

item.title: Análise: está na hora de rediscutir as indicações de ministros do STF?
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF highlights the tension between technical merit and political alliances in the appointment process, as the Brazilian Constitution requires presidential nomination and senatorial approval, making the role inherently political. The analysis argues that this structure favors ministers with strong political ties, such as Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes, leading to perceptions of politicization and weakening the Court’s legitimacy in public opinion.

item.title: Após barrar Messias no STF, Senado terá 27 nomes de Lula para analisar em 2026
item.description: The Lula government has up to 27 nominations for regulatory agency boards, the Central Bank, CADE, and CVM in 2026, all requiring Senate Federal approval. The recent rejection of a Supreme Court nominee increases the risk of delays in this process, particularly as several mandates expire later this year. Vacancies exist in the Central Bank (two seats), CADE (three vacancies, including the presidency), and other agencies, with some positions currently filled on an interim basis.

item.title: Acabou ou não?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro claimed that Lula's government has ended, sparking debate among readers of Blog do Noblat. A poll of 1,168 participants revealed that 82.6% believe Lula will be re-elected, while 17.4% agree with Bolsonaro's statement.

item.title: Como os clãs familiares atravessam a disputa ao governo em estados do Nordeste
item.description: In the 2026 elections, Brazil's Northeast continues to see strong influence of political dynasties in the race for state governorships, with candidates like João Campos (Pernambuco), Orleans Brandão (Maranhão), Renan Filho (Alagoas) and ACM Neto (Bahia) leveraging inherited political capital from previous generations. These families maintain control over party structures, resources, and electoral networks despite shifts in party allegiance and the rise of new political forces such as the PT. Although most visible in the Northeast, this pattern reflects a national trend of power perpetuation through familial ties and institutional legacy.

item.title: Aumenta a torcida para que Lula desista de se candidatar à reeleição
item.description: Brazilian media and parts of the elite are urging President Lula to abandon his 2026 re-election bid, despite polls not determining electoral outcomes. The article notes that media influence on elections has been inconsistent historically, and Lula has previously won against media opposition in 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, and 2022. Despite pressure, Lula remains in the race, and the scenario could shift if figures like Ronaldo Caiado or Romeu Zema gain traction by August 2026.

item.title: Tarcísio aposta em nova dobradinha com Nunes para vencer PT na capital
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) aims to renew his alliance with Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) for the 2026 elections, reversing roles: Nunes will act as an active campaign surrogate for Tarcísio in the capital to weaken the PT and overturn the 2022 defeat, when Haddad won 54.5% to 45.5%. The strategy leverages São Paulo’s electoral weight — 9 million voters, 26.8% of the state — and reinforces Tarcísio’s image as a leader in urban revitalization and public safety, exemplified by the 'Times Square Paulistana' project.

item.title: Nova presidente do TRF-1 já teve redes suspensas por apoiar atos golpistas em quartéis
item.description: The new president of the TRF-1, Maria do Carmo Cardoso, had her Instagram and X accounts suspended by the CNJ in 2022 for publicly supporting coup-related acts in front of Army barracks, including a post after the 2022 World Cup elimination stating 'our true team is in front of the barracks'. Despite claiming she did not remember the post, the case was archived in 2023 by an eight-to-six vote. She is close to the Bolsonaro clan and served as godmother to the appointment of Kassio Nunes Marques to the STF.

item.title: Além de Flávio, outro presidenciável mira Zema como vice
item.description: In addition to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Goiás former governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), a pre-candidate for president under the same party, also expressed interest in having former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) as his running mate. Both acknowledge that Zema is unlikely to abandon his presidential bid after his confrontation with STF Minister Gilmar Mendes, but PL leaders believe the conflict may temporarily boost his poll numbers, making him more open to accepting a vice-presidential role.

item.title: Juiz nega pedido para excluir post de Nikolas sobre Janja e Lula
item.description: The judge of the 6th Special Civil Court of Brasília denied an urgent request to remove Nikolas Ferreira's social media post about Janja's reaction to Lula hugging a supporter, stating there was no reference to the plaintiff's transgender identity or incitement to hatred. The lawsuit was filed by Manuella Tyler, a transgender council substitute from Juazeiro (BA), who claimed she suffered transphobic hate speech after the post went viral. The judge noted that, amid extreme political polarization, the content may provoke criticism but does not constitute illegality warranting immediate removal.

item.title: Boneco de Bolsonaro e 'sem anistia': intervenção de militantes rivais gera confusão em atos do 1º de Maio no DF e em SP
item.description: Labor Day protests saw clashes in Brasília and São Paulo. In Brasília, a CUT-organized event turned violent when Bolsonaro supporters displayed a life-size doll of the ex-president, seen as a provocation. In São Paulo, bolsonarista demonstrators on Avenida Paulista faced chants of 'no amnesty', leading to a woman being shoved and injured, while the rally was authorized by the mayor and police, disrupting traditional left-wing occupations.

item.title: Contra o 'andar de cima': pressionado nas pesquisas e pelo Congresso, Lula tenta reação com resgate de discurso antissistema
item.description: Facing congressional defeats and stagnating polls, President Lula invoked an anti-system discourse for the first time in a national broadcast, aiming to reverse his image and boost re-election prospects in 2026. The move, previously signaled by PT leaders like Edinho Silva and Gleisi Hoffmann, seeks to reconnect with his 2022 base by attacking the 'top floor' as a symbol of elite privilege and disconnection from the people.

item.title: Haddad insinua que o povo está desorientado: 'lavagem cerebral'
item.description: Fernando Haddad suggested that the Brazilian people are suffering from 'brainwashing', attributing Lula's poor performance in electoral polls to public disorientation during Workers' Day. He called it 'inadmissible' that President Lula is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro in the polls, implying that public perception is distorted by manipulation.

item.title: Em crise nos bastidores, Botafogo tenta seguir em alta dentro de campo
item.description: Botafogo faces a severe financial crisis with R$2 billion in debt, but performs strongly on the pitch, boasting nine unbeaten matches and rising to eighth in the Brasileirão with 17 points. Key players Danilo, Alex Telles, and Vitinho are in contention for Brazil’s 2026 World Cup squad, while young attacker Kudir may be called up by Panama. For today’s match against Remo, Botafogo will miss Alexander Barboza, who is in advanced talks with Palmeiras, and is expected to field Bastos and Ferraresi in defense.

item.title: Inflação de alimentos põe em xeque bondades eleitorais de Lula
item.description: President Lula is seeking re-election through voter benefits packages, similar to Bolsonaro and Dilma, but faces high rejection: 40% negative approval according to Datafolha, five months before the first round. He is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro in second-round projections, as food inflation erodes his political capital.

item.title: Pequenas mesquinharias têm grandes consequências no caso Messias
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF, led by Flávio Bolsonaro and backed by 28 senators, exposed the fragility of Lula’s government before Congress, weakened presidential authority, and hindered the passage of key projects like the 6x1 work schedule, five months before the 2026 elections. The opposition celebrated the outcome as a political victory, reinforcing narratives against 'Supreme Court excesses' and directly benefiting Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy, while threatening Romeu Zema’s (Novo) agenda.

item.title: Congresso confirma tradição golpista
item.description: The National Congress reaffirmed its coup-prone tradition by supporting the overturning of Lula's full veto on the Dosimetry Law, attacking the legal framework protecting the Democratic State of Law approved in 2021. The move, driven by Bolsonarism and allies, was summarized by historian Carlos Fico as another episode in Brazil's tradition of bulldozing democracy.

item.title: Zema defende que crianças possam trabalhar no Brasil: 'Nós vamos mudar'
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential pre-candidate from the Novo party, advocated for relaxing Brazil's ban on child labor, arguing that children should be allowed to work in simple tasks from a young age, as he did at five helping his father. He blamed the left for promoting the idea that work harms children and pledged to change the current law prohibiting work for those under 16 if elected.

item.title: Associação de familiares diz que PL da dosimetria vai beneficiar 600 condenados pelo 8/1
item.description: The Association of Relatives and Victims of January 8 (Asfav) claims that approximately 600 individuals convicted for the January 8 riots will benefit from the so-called dosimetry bill, following the overturning of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) full veto. The proposal aims to adjust sentences based on proportionality and individualized punishment criteria.

item.title: Advogados de réus da trama golpista temem que judicialização atrase redução das penas
item.description: Lawyers for those convicted in the January 8 coup plot are preparing requests for sentence reduction based on the Dosimetria Bill, but fear that judicialization of the issue at the STF will delay analysis of these requests. The strategy aims to apply more lenient criteria proposed in the bill, still under consideration.

item.title: Petrobras defende Lula, critica distribuidoras e diz não ter mais postos
item.description: Petrobras aired a national advertisement on open TV stating it no longer controls fuel stations, as its distribution operations were privatized in 2021 with the sale of BR Distribuidora (Vibra Energia). The company attributes final fuel prices to distributor margins and the impact of the Middle East war, noting that gasoline sold to distributors has not increased since 2024 and that the government is acting to reduce diesel prices, which have risen over 20% since the conflicts began.

item.title: Cidade de Cascavel, no Paraná, recebe a segunda etapa da Nascar Brasil
item.description: Cascavel, in Paraná, will host the second stage of the 2026 Nascar Brazil season, one of nine scheduled events for the year. The announcement was made by RedeTV! News on May 1, 2026, emphasizing the event's significance for Brazil's motorsport scene.

item.title: Chuvas em Pernambuco deixam quatro mortos e cinco feridos
item.description: Heavy rains in Pernambuco left four dead and five injured between January 30 and February 1, with victims being two mothers and their children in Olinda and Recife. The state government confirmed 340 rescues by the Fire Department and issued severe-level alerts for five municipalities. President Lula declared federal support, including emergency recognition and deployment of National Civil Defense and National Health System (SUS) teams.

item.title: Edinho diz que Flávio quer entregar terras-raras aos EUA
item.description: Edinho Silva, president of the Workers' Party, accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of intending to deliver Brazil's rare earth reserves to the United States, claiming it undermines national sovereignty. He reinforced Lula's pre-candidacy as the leader best prepared for global turmoil and used the issue in a social media video to amplify criticism. Edinho also criticized the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' STF nomination and the overturning of the presidential veto on reducing penalties for the January 8 attacks.

item.title: Após derrota no Congresso, governo aposta em pressão dos trabalhadores para tentar derrubar escala 6x1
item.description: The Lula government is betting on worker pressure — particularly through May Day rallies in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro — to push Congress to abolish the 6x1 work schedule before the 2026 elections. Government officials urged society to mobilize deputies and senators in support of reducing the workweek.

item.title: Fortes chuvas deixam quatro mortos em Pernambuco, segundo Defesa Civil
item.description: Heavy rains left four dead and affected 403 people in Pernambuco, causing landslides, building collapses, and flooding in Recife, Olinda, and seven other municipalities. Over 200 mm of rain in 12 hours raised the Capibaribe River level, leaving 32 families displaced and 93 homeless. President Lula mobilized federal support, including the National Civil Defense and the National SUS Force, after speaking with João Campos and Humberto Costa.

item.title: Haddad e ministros participam de ato do 1° de Maio no ABC e cobram Congresso por fim da escala 6x1
item.description: At the May Day event in São Bernardo do Campo, Fernando Haddad and Lula’s ministers urged Congress to approve a 40-hour workweek without salary reduction, emphasizing the need for worker mobilization ahead of the October elections. Haddad also revealed that the PT is negotiating with unions the platform for Lula’s next term, including tax exemption on profit-sharing (PLR) as a key demand.

item.title: Chuvas: Governo envia Defesa Civil para Pernambuco e Paraíba
item.description: The federal government deployed National Civil Defense teams to support Pernambuco and Paraíba following heavy rains causing flooding and landslide risks. The action was ordered by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, coordinated by Minister Waldez Góes, to assist in emergency recognition and impact mitigation. In Pernambuco, seven municipalities are on alert, with rainfall exceeding 100 mm in 24h, highlighting Goiana (181 mm) and Abreu e Lima (144,8 mm).

item.title: Confusões e pouca gente marcaram os atos da direita na Paulista no 1/5
item.description: Right-wing demonstrations on Paulista Avenue on May 1st drew fewer than 100 people, were marked by clashes and confrontations with pedestrians, including shoving and verbal aggression. The 'Patriotas do QG' group used a sound truck featuring Bolsonaro effigies and a 'Uncle Sam' figure wearing a hybrid U.S.-Brazil flag outfit, but lacked participation from top conservative leaders.

item.title: Os nomes mais atingidos no governo Lula após derrota de Messias no Congresso
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court exposed serious flaws in the Lula government's political articulation, despite prior warnings from Senate allies about the lack of sufficient votes. The defeat was seen as a political score-settling, damaging the government's credibility and putting pressure on key figures such as Jaques Wagner, Randolfe Rodrigues, and José Guimarães, who are now facing criticism from both the coalition and the PT base.

item.title: Nova campanha do PT mira escala 6x1, mulheres e trabalhadores por app
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) launched a new campaign titled 'First You', focused on labor issues for Workers' Day. The initiative includes videos addressing the end of the 6×1 work schedule, regulation of app-based workers, and the impact of professional life on women, highlighting overload and double shifts.
